newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen rising towards recent high of 124.41.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen rising towards recent high of 124.41.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to rise towards its recent high of 124.41 on Monday, traders said.

The September should be firmly underpinned at around 124.00 after sentiment turned bullish on Friday after the Japanese Trade Ministry's weaker-than-expected forecasts for industrial production in June and July, they said.

"The contract may stay range-bound today ahead of a six-year JGB auction on Tuesday. But there is little downside risk after Friday's sharp recovery above the 124.00 level," said a dealer at a domestic securities house.

But further rises would be difficult without cash bond buying by investors, traders said. They said they expect the contract to move between 123.80 and 124.40 after Friday's Tokyo close of 124.15. On LIFFE, it closed at 124.18.

"Both the tankan (the Bank of Japan's quarterly corporate sentiment survey) and industrial output data showed that the current economic recovery is strong, although it is expected to be weaker in the near future. This should curb further rises," said a market analyst at a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said a focus would be whether the Nikkei stock average manages to rise to the key 21,000 level.
